subject: Calypso-3B — elevated 5xx/timeouts: customer update & closure
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@stormline.io>, Stormline SRE <sre@stormline.io>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Calypso-3B — transient elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting stormline-prod

Hi Asha / Stormline SRE team,

Quick heads up: between ~2027-01-08 13:45 and 15:10 PST we observed a sharp increase in 5xx and timeout errors for requests routed to the Calypso-3B model under your stormline-prod workspace. Symptoms we saw:
- Total 5xx rate rose from ~0.2% baseline to ~6.8% (spike concentrated on requests with long prompt prefixes / sequence lengths > 1k tokens)
- Increased generator timeouts (client saw 30s+ stalls)
- A subset of requests returned 5xx with kernel-level tracebacks on our side

Impact: user-facing errors on a small percentage of API calls (we estimate ~0.6% of end-user sessions experienced a visible error during the window).

Immediate mitigation we applied:
1) Traffic routing: we automatically routed your production traffic to Calypso-3B-v2 (quantized fallback variant) where compatible — this reduced the 5xx rate to ~0.6% within 10 minutes.
2) Inflight throttle: short-lived rate controls on the busiest routes to prevent cache thrash.
3) Ops action: rolling restart of the affected inference pool and a targeted kernel patch pushed to the runtime on the impacted nodes.

Ticket: Redwood-INC-9876 (we'll keep this open until final RCA). I've attached an incident summary and we've looped in infra and runtime owners (cc).

ETA / next steps: we'll follow up by EOD (PST) tomorrow with an RCA and permanent remediation plan; meanwhile routing remains on the fallback and we continue monitoring.

Sorry for the disruption — I'll follow up with more detail shortly.

Best,
Irene

Subject: Internal: Calypso-3B spike — technical findings and next steps

Team — summary of the technical investigation so far (internal notes, sharing to keep customer thread updated):

Root cause (initial):
- We traced the failures to a kernel-codepath mismatch that only surfaces under a narrow distribution of inputs: long prefix lengths (>1k tokens) combined with a specific KV cache eviction pattern in Calypso-3B compiled with the older quantization kernels.
- Under load this caused excessive KV cache thrashing and memory pressure on the inference nodes; the runtime started returning 5xx when the kernel attempted a fallback that threw an unexpected OOM-like trace.

Why did fallback not handle gracefully?
- The runtime's kernel selection logic did not escalate to the cold-path safely for this kernel variant; this exposed an uncovered edge-case in quantized attention kernels.

What we did (mitigation already applied):
1) Immediate traffic split: routed stormline-prod to calypso-3b-v2 (quantized variant with newer kernels) — reduced 5xx from 6.8% -> 0.6% in ~10m.
2) Live kernel patch: deployed a guard in the kernel selector to force the safe cold-path for affected calls. Rolling restart completed across 75% of the affected pool by 09:40 PST.
3) Telemetry: enabled extra tracing for sequence length buckets to detect recurrence.

Longer-term remediation (action items):
- Backport kernel selector guard to all quantized families (owner: runtime/kernel team; ETA: 2027-01-14)
- Add model-level circuit breaker to detect this exact failure mode and failover earlier (owner: serving runtime; ETA: 2027-01-21)
- Add a regression test in our model onboarding CI that reproduces the sequence-length cache pattern (owner: model team; ETA: 2027-01-18)

Attachments for internal review: kernel-trace.log, fallback-config.json

I'll coordinate the RCA write-up; Irene, please feel free to cut a short customer-facing summary from this and share the closure note with Stormline.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Calypso-3B — recovery confirmed, root cause summary, and next steps

Hi Asha / Alec / Stormline SRE —

Thanks again for your patience while our team investigated. Final update and next steps:

What happened (plain language):
- A low-level kernel incompatibility in our quantized execution path caused some Calypso-3B requests with very long prompts to fail under sustained traffic. That codepath triggered elevated 5xx/timeouts for a short window on Jan 8.

What we did to recover:
- Immediately routed your traffic to a compatible Calypso-3B fallback variant; that restored normal request success rates within ~10 minutes.
- Applied a runtime guard and performed a rolling restart of the affected inference pool. The routing to fallback is no longer required — we have rebalanced your traffic back to the primary pool and are observing steady success rates (5xx ~0.1% over the last 4h, within expected baseline).

Impact summary:
- Window: ~2027-01-08 13:45–15:10 PST
- Estimated user sessions affected: ~0.6% of active sessions during the window; we captured request ids and traces where available and will provide them if you want a per-request checklist.

Remediation and prevention:
- We will backport the kernel-selector safe-path guard across quantized families (ETA 2027-01-14).
- We'll add model-level circuit breakers to detect similar failures early (ETA 2027-01-21).
- We are adding a targeted CI regression for the sequence-length/KV pattern.

Compensation: we will issue a service credit equivalent to one week of usage for the affected routes. I'll have your account team open a credit request and confirm details tomorrow.

Postmortem: a concise RCA is published here: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/calypso-3b-20270108 (attached: calypso-rca-summary.pdf).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the RCA and action items — happy to set that up for this week.

Apologies for the disruption; please let me know if you want the full per-request traces and we'll share via the secure link.

Best,
Irene
